title: 𓂋𓄿 𓏌𓅱 𓉐𓂋𓏏𓂻 𓅓 𓉔𓂋𓅱𓇳
titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 15, the hymns (part 4 of 4)
part: Spell 15 — the hymns, part 4 of 4: the last titles of Ra, Ani's prayer to be glorified and to sail in the Field of Reeds, and promises of his voyage with the sun (Plate 21)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plate XXI. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 135–137; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: The fourth and last part of Spell 15 ends Ani's hymn to Ra on Plate 21. The list of the god's titles closes, and Ani prays that he be glorified in the necropolis, placed among the revered ones, joined with the bas in the Sacred Land and allowed to sail in the Field of Reeds. A last section, opened by a word written in red, promises him that he will cross the sky among the stars, see Ra in his shrine, the inet-fish and the abdju-fish, and Horus, and Thoth and Maat at his sides, while the enemy falls and all the gods rejoice. Budge's type is uncertain in many signs here, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.i: Great of dread, power of the powers, whose seat is far(?) from the wrongdoers;
sentences.n: ꜥꜣ nrw 'great of dread' is the column ꜥꜣ with U15 (read ꜥ, as throughout these plates), the vulture ꜣ and the roll, then nrw 'dread' spelled out sign by sign (n-r-w-i-w; the i and the second w are not read): water n, r, the chick w, a reed and the coil w (a fuller spelling), with U15 and plural strokes as classifiers, where the word usually has the vulture (G14) that classifies it (Spell 17 on this papyrus also writes nrw without the vulture); Budge's numeral 35 stands inside it. 'Great of X' is an adjective with the thing it is great in. sḫm sḫmw 'power of the powers' is the sceptre sḫm with m and U15, then the sceptre again with a stroke and the seated god for the divine 'Powers': a noun followed by its own plural, 'the mightiest of the mighty'. ḥrw st·f r isftyw is taken as ḥri 'be far (from: r)', 'far is his seat from the wrongdoers', taken as a participle with the noun after it, 'far of seat', the same pattern as ꜥꜣ nrw: the face ḥr with r, w and U15, then st 'seat' (the seat Q1, t and a house sign) with ·f; Budge reads ḥeru, 'fortifying', and the reading is doubtful. isftyw 'wrongdoers' is i, the tall sign is (coded Y1a, approximate, as in isft), s, f, t and the vulture standing for the plural ending, as in ḫftyw, with a kneeling man struck on the head (A14, approximate) as classifier. The list of the sun-god's titles from the previous part goes on.

sentences.n: ꜥꜣ ḫꜥw has the same pattern: ḫꜥw 'appearings' is the sun rising over a hill (N28) with ꜥ, w, the roll and a stroke, the god's shining forth. sktt, the evening bark (s, k, t twice and a boat on a stand, P3, approximate), and ꜥḏt, the morning bark (the netting needle ꜥḏ, V26, approximate, with t twice, the hand d and the boat; the short name the first part of the spell also has for the Mandjet-bark), are the barks of the sun's two journeys. wr·f is the swallow wr with r and ·f: 'great is he', the sḏm·f of the adjective-verb wr 'be great' with ·f as its subject (an adjectival sentence would have the dependent pronoun, wr sw). ꜣw after it is the spine with a cord at each end (F40) with w, the roll and a stroke, 'long, extended'; how it is joined to wr·f is not clear (Budge: āu, 'exceedingly'), and the rendering is doubtful. sentences.l: see · behind · you · wrong
sentences.i: See, wrong is behind you(?).
sentences.n: mk 'see, behold' is the owl m with the arm (G17 and D36 printed as one ligature, approximate; m is often written mꜥ on this papyrus, and the arm is not read) and k. ḥꜣ·k 'behind you' is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with ꜣ and the back of the head (D1, approximate): the preposition ḥꜣ with ·k. isft 'wrong' is spelled as in isftyw above, with the sparrow and plural strokes. There is no verb: as it stands this is an adverbial sentence with the predicate put first, 'behind you is wrong' (after mk the subject usually comes first, mk isft ḥꜣ·k, so the order is unusual), that is, wrong is put out of the god's sight. Budge supplies a verb and a 'his' ('put behind thee [his] faults'; the [his] is in his English only). The sense is doubtful.

sentences.i: May you place me among the revered ones, with the spirits.
sentences.n: Budge's ṭā-kuà is one group; it is split here into di·k 'may you place' and wi 'me': the kneeling man (A1) alone writes the dependent pronoun wi, the object of rdi, as in mk-wi elsewhere on the papyrus. rdi m is 'put among'. The signs can also be read as one word, Budge's group: di·kwi, the stative of rdi with the 1st-person ending ·kwi written k and the seated man (as in nn·kwi elsewhere on the papyrus), 'I am placed among the revered ones'; both readings fit the signs, and the split is doubtful. imꜣḫyw 'the revered ones' is the spine with one hanging cord (F39), the imꜣḫ sign, with ḫ and two reeds y: the plural of imꜣḫy 'one honoured', the blessed dead who are provided for (Budge: àmχi); his numeral 38 stands inside it. ḫr 'with, near' is the placenta ḫ and r, the preposition used of persons. ꜣḫw 'the spirits' is the ibis ꜣḫ (G25, approximate) with ḫ, a kneeling figure holding a flail (A52, approximate) and a stroke. Ani speaks of himself here as 'me', and in the next clause again as 'he'.

sentences.n: ḫnm·f 'may he be joined (with)' is the jug ḫnm (W9) with m, the roll and ·f, a sḏm·f of wish; ḫnm takes the ones joined as its object. bꜣw 'the bas' is the incense bowl (R7), the ba's classifier on these plates, with the ram bꜣ (E10, approximate) and two strokes, as in the second part of the spell. tꜣ-ḏsr 'the Sacred Land' is the strip of land tꜣ (N16, approximate), then a low sign coded U15 (approximate) that stands where the arm with the wand of ḏsr (D45) is expected, t twice and the hill-land. sentences.i: may he sail in the Field of Reeds, because protection(?) has been decreed with gladness of heart.
sentences.n: sqdd·f 'may he sail' is the bolt s, the tall sign qd (Aa28, approximate), the hand d twice (Budge: seqṭeṭ), a small pot (W24, approximate; not read) and the boat on a stand as classifiers, and ·f: sqdi 'travel by boat', a sḏm·f taken as a wish like ḫnm·f before it. The hand is written twice, as in sqdt for the Sektet-bark in the previous part; it may be only a spelling, or the doubled form (sqdd·f) of this 3ae-inf verb, which is not usually the form of a wish, and the reading of the form is doubtful. sḫt-iꜣrw 'the Field of Reeds' is the field with t and the wedge (N21, approximate), then i, ꜣ, r, w with the reed plant, strokes and the town sign; Budge's numeral 39 stands inside it. Budge prints ḥer enti sa as three groups under one English word, 'through'. ḥr and nty are joined here into ḥr-ntt 'because' (the face with its stroke, n, t and the two strokes for the ending, as elsewhere on this papyrus), and sꜣ is read as a noun of its own: a box-like sign with a loop (coded Aa17, approximate; the protection sign V16/V17 is possible) with a stroke, taken as sꜣ 'protection'; this rests on an uncertain sign. wḏ is the staff wḏ (V24, approximate) with w and the roll, 'is decreed', the stative after its subject sꜣ, the usual pattern after ḥr-ntt (noun + stative). ꜣwt-ib 'gladness of heart' is the spine ꜣw (F40) with t and the heart: literally 'length of heart'. The clause after ḥr-ntt is doubtful as a whole.

sentences.i: So says the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice.
sentences.n: in, the reed and water, is taken here as 'says': in with a noun after the words quoted names the speaker, 'says N', and closes Ani's prayer. In Spells 18 and 146 in N stands before the words it introduces; here the words that follow speak to Ani as 'you', so it is taken as closing what comes before. Budge renders it 'O', a call that would open the address that follows; the call is usually i (as at the start of the previous part), so that reading is less likely, but it is possible, and this is doubtful. Budge's 'joy of heart' runs on under in; it belongs to ꜣwt-ib alone. Wsir is written short, the seat (Q2, approximate) over the eye with no god classifier; sš 'the scribe' is the palette alone (Y3, approximate); mꜣꜥ-ḫrw without the sickle, as before.

sentences.n: mꜣꜣ·n·k 'you have seen' is the eye with the sickle mꜣ printed above it, the vulture twice, n and ·k: the sḏm·n·f, written so three times in this passage (Budge: maa-nek, 'thou shalt see'); the past tense stands among promises in the future, and it is kept as written; Budge's numeral 43 stands inside it. int 'the inet-fish' is i, the fish in, n, t and a second fish as classifier (both K1, approximate). ḫpr·s 'its coming into being' is the scarab ḫpr with r, a reed, a standing mummy-shaped figure (A53, approximate), the roll and a stroke as classifiers, and ·s (the bolt): the infinitive with a suffix for its subject. bꜥbꜥt is the foot b with ꜥ (U15), twice, and t over three water lines: a word for water (Budge: bābāt, 'the water'), not met in the earlier parts; its sense is doubtful. nt 'of' is n and t; mfkꜣt 'turquoise' is the owl with the arm (as in mk), f, k, t and a small round stone classifier with plural strokes; the ꜣ is not written. sentences.i: May it come about that evil falls … as he has foretold(?).
sentences.n: ḫpr is the scarab with r: 'may it come about', a wish, with what follows as its content. ḏwt 'evil' is the mountain ḏw (N26, approximate) with t and w, followed by one sign that Budge prints as a row of small hanging looped strands, for which there is no good code (D3, approximate, as in ḫfty below); it stands where the sparrow of bad things would be (Budge: ṭutu, 'the Evil One'). ḫr 'fall' is ḫ, r and a falling man (A15); ḏwt ḫr, noun then verb, is taken as the content of the wish, 'that evil falls'; the form of ḫr is not clear: a stative after the feminine ḏwt would usually show its ending t, which is not written here. Before ḫr the sign line has an empty space, and Budge's transliteration has dots ('.....') there; he prints no signs and no brackets, so nothing is read or restored, but something may be missing. ḫft 'as, according as' is ḫ, f, t; sr·n·f 'he has foretold' is s, r and the giraffe sr (E27) with n and ·f: the sḏm·n·f of sr 'foretell, make known'. Budge reads 'when he setteth in order'; who 'he' is is not said, and the rendering is doubtful.

sentences.n: sk is s, then a twisted cord crossed by a bowed bar with knotted ends (coded V28 as elsewhere in these plates, but with the bar of the swab sk, V29), k and U15; then water n with a stroke. Budge prints sek and en as two groups; they are joined here into sk·n, the sḏm·n·f of sk with sktt 'the Sektet-bark' as its noun subject, as in the first part of the spell (sktt sk·n·s pḥ sw), where the same words stand: 'the Sektet-bark has hauled'. sentences.i: You have seen Horus at the neferu(?), and Thoth and Maat on either side of him.
sentences.n: mꜣꜣ·n·k is written here with one vulture. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon alone. ḥr nfrw: the face ḥr with its stroke is 'at, upon'; nfrw is the nfr sign with f, r, w, a kneeling man with an arm raised to his face (A2, approximate) and a flat bar with a small hanging tuft (Aa13, approximate) over plural strokes. Budge prints '(?)' over that bar in the sign line, unsure of the sign himself, and renders 'the place of look out'; the word is left untranslated here as 'the neferu(?)', and its sense is unknown. Thoth's name has no ibis (G26): it is spelled out with the hand d (standing for ḏ, as in later spellings), ḥ, w, t, y and the seated god. mꜣꜥt 'Maat' is the plinth with t and the goddess with the feather (C10, approximate). ḥr ꜥwy·f 'at his two arms' is the dual of ꜥ 'arm': U15 (standing for the arm ꜥ), a stroke and U15 again, y and w, with ·f and the two strokes of the dual after it, which are not read; Budge's numeral 48 stands inside it. Thoth and Maat stand on either side of the god in the bark.

sentences.n: in is here the reed with the fish trap in (W25, approximate), another spelling of the word in line 39, and it is taken the same way, 'says N', closing the hymn; Budge gives it no English, and it is doubtful. It is less easy here than in line 39: the promises before it speak to Ani as 'you', so 'says N' must mean that Ani recites them for himself. Ani's title follows: sš ḥtp-nṯr 'scribe of the god's offerings'. Budge prints ḥetep and neter as two groups under one English ('of the divine offerings'); they are joined here into ḥtp-nṯr, the offering table with t and p and the flag with the seated god. n nbw wꜣst 'of the lords of Thebes' is n, the basket nb with plural strokes, and Waset, the sceptre wꜣs (R19, approximate) with t and the town sign. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw without the sickle. ḥnꜥ·sn 'with them' is ḥ, n, ꜥ with ·sn (here with the folded cloth s): Ani is among the gods and spirits just named. Spell 15 ends here; in Budge's edition Spell 133 begins on the next page.

glossary.ḫnm: ḫnm — to smell; to be joined with (verb); here, doubtfully, as a noun "companion, friend"
glossary.bꜣ: bꜣ — ba, soul; the Ram, the ba-ram of Mendes (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: to hack open, break open (?) (verb; written like the word for the ba, with a knife as classifier; the sense is doubtful; Budge: ba, 'pass through')
glossary.tꜣ-ḏsr: tꜣ-ḏsr — 'the Sacred Land', the cemetery, realm of Osiris (place name m.; tꜣ 'land' + ḏsr 'holy'; Budge: Ta-sert)
glossary.sqdi: sqdi — to sail, travel by boat (verb 3ae-inf.; geminated stem sqdd; Budge: seqṭeṭ)
glossary.sḫt-iꜣrw: sḫt-iꜣrw — the Field of Reeds, the fertile land of the blessed dead (place name f.; sḫt 'field' + iꜣrw 'reeds'; Budge: Seχet-Àrui)
glossary.ḥr-ntt: ḥr-ntt — because (conjunction: ḥr 'on account of' + ntt 'that')
glossary.sꜣ: sꜣ — protection (noun; m sꜣ "for the protection of") · a second word of the same spelling: son (noun m.; the pintail-duck sign; sꜣ·k 'your son', sꜣ tpy 'eldest son') · a third word of the same spelling: back (noun; the sign Aa18; as in m-sꜣ 'behind'; Budge: sa)
glossary.wḏ: wḏ — to command, decree, ordain (verb) · also wḏt 'command, decree' (noun f., from the verb) · also wḏ 'command, decree' (noun m.)
glossary.ꜣwt-ib: ꜣwt-ib — joy, gladness; literally 'length of heart' (compound noun f.; ꜣwt 'length', from ꜣwi 'be long', + ib 'heart'; Budge: āut)
glossary.in: in — by (naming the agent, as in ḏd in N "said by N"); (particle) it is … · a second word of the same spelling: to say, said (verb; normally after the words quoted: in·sn 'they say', in N 'says N'; in·k 'you said') · also the interrogative particle, in iw 'is it that …?' opening a question (Budge: àn àu)
glossary.sš: sš — scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here) · also to write, draw, paint (verb; written with the scribe's palette) · also the noun 'writing, document, record' (noun m.) · also to open (a door), spread open (verb; said of doors and bolts) · a further word of the same spelling: nest (noun m.; written with the nest of young birds; dual sšwy)
glossary.pri: pri — to go out, come forth (verb)
glossary.biꜣ: biꜣ — iron, metal (noun m.; biꜣ n pt 'iron of heaven', metal fallen from the sky; Budge: bàat) · also the firmament, the sky thought of as a vault of metal (noun m.; Budge: bàt)
glossary.snsn: snsn — to smell, breathe (verb; reduplicated from sn "smell, kiss") · also to join, keep company with, associate with (verb; with m or m-m 'among'; Budge: sensen)
glossary.m-m: m-m — among, in the midst of (compound preposition; later spelled with ꜥ)
glossary.sbꜣ: sbꜣ — door, gate (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: star (noun m.; written with the star sign; plural sbꜣw)
glossary.ir: ir — to do, make (lemma iri) · a second word of the same spelling: the particle ir "when, if" at the head of a clause (ir ꜥq·i "when I entered"), here apparently also bringing in a question ("do you know …?") · also "as for" (particle; ir with a noun puts that noun first as the topic) · also irt, what is done, deeds (noun f.; from iri 'do'; irt·k 'your deeds')
glossary.·tw: ·tw — one, someone (impersonal suffix; makes a passive: ḏd·tw 'one says, it is said')
glossary.n: n — not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …' · the preposition also 'because of, on account of'
glossary.ḥknw: ḥknw — praise, hymns of praise (noun m.; from ḥkn 'praise'; Budge: ḥekennu)
glossary.wiꜣ: wiꜣ — boat, bark, especially of a god (noun)
glossary.nis: nis — to call, summon, call out (a name) (verb)
glossary.dgi: dgi — to look, look at, behold (verb; also written dgg)
glossary.rꜥ: rꜥ — Ra, the sun-god (god's name; Budge: Rā) · also the sun; day (noun; rꜥ nb 'every day')
glossary.ẖnw: ẖnw — the inside, interior, residence (noun; m ẖnw 'within')
glossary.ny: ny — of (the genitive adjective; written n, fem. nt, pl. nw): rꜣ n ꜥq "spell of entering"
glossary.kꜣri: kꜣri — shrine, chapel (noun m.; Budge: kerà)
glossary.sḥtp: sḥtp — to make content, satisfy, appease (verb; causative of ḥtp 'be content')
glossary.itn: itn — the disk of the sun, the Aten (noun)
glossary.hrw: hrw — terror, dread · a second word of the same spelling: day (noun; plural hrww)
glossary.nb: nb — lord, master, possessor (of); (adjective, after a noun) every, all
glossary.sḏm·n·f: sḏm·n·f — the n of the sḏm·n·f, marking a completed action ("I have …", "I …ed") (verb form; written between the verb and its suffix)
glossary.int: int — the inet-fish, a kind of fish (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: valley, wadi (noun f.)
glossary.ḫpr: ḫpr — to come into being, happen, become (verb)
glossary.·s: ·s — she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)
glossary.ḥr: ḥr — face; (preposition) upon, on, over, concerning · a second word of the same spelling: Horus, the falcon god, son of Osiris and Isis; the sun as a falcon (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru) · also 'at' (ḥr sbꜣw 'at the gates'); ḥr-tp 'upon' (compound preposition: ḥr + tp 'head') · also for, on behalf of; on account of (preposition; ḥr·k 'for you') · also 'with' (of the cause of a feeling: ḥtp ḥr·s 'content with it')
glossary.bꜥbꜥt: bꜥbꜥt — water (?) (noun f.; a reduplicated word; sense doubtful, taken from Budge: bābāt, 'the water')
glossary.mfkꜣt: mfkꜣt — turquoise (noun f.; Budge: māfkia, which he renders 'emerald')
glossary.ꜣbḏw: ꜣbḏw — Abydos, the holy city of Osiris (place name; Budge: Àbṭu) · a second word of the same spelling: the abdju-fish (noun; a fish that swims before the sun's bark)
glossary.sp: sp — time, occasion; deed, case, matter (noun); sp sn 'twice'
glossary.ḫft: ḫft — in front of, facing; in accordance with; at the time of, when (preposition; also before a verb form)
glossary.sr: sr — official, magistrate, noble (noun; plural srw) · a second word of the same spelling: to foretell, make known (verb; Budge: sert)
glossary.ḥsq: ḥsq — to cut off (verb; written with the knife as classifier; perhaps also of cutting grain, reaping (?); Budge: ḥesq)
glossary.·i: ·i — I, me (1st-person singular suffix pronoun; the seated-man sign)
glossary.dm: dm — to be sharp; to pierce, cut (verb; Budge: ṭemu)
glossary.ṯst: ṯst — vertebra, backbone (noun f.; from ṯs 'tie'; Budge: θest, 'the vertebræ')
glossary.mꜣꜥw: mꜣꜥw — fair wind (noun m.; Budge: maāu)
glossary.nfr: nfr — beautiful, good, perfect (adjective; follows its noun; verb 'be good'); also beauty, goodness (noun m.)
glossary.sk: sk — to wipe, sweep (verb); perhaps also to drag, tow (?) (sense uncertain; Budge's 'toweth') · a second word of the same spelling: to perish (verb; skt after tm 'not perishing'; the Imperishable Stars iḫmw-sk are 'those who do not know perishing')
glossary.pḥ: pḥ — to reach, arrive at, attain (verb)
glossary.sw: sw — he, him, it (3rd person masculine singular dependent pronoun)
glossary.qdt: qdt — crew, sailors (?) (noun f., collective; reading and sense doubtful, taken from Budge: qet, 'the sailors')
glossary.nbt-ꜥnḫ: nbt-ꜥnḫ — 'Lady of Life', a name or title of a goddess (god's name f.; nbt 'lady' + ꜥnḫ 'life'; Budge: Nebt-ānχ)
glossary.nḏm: nḏm — to be sweet, pleasant (verb; nḏm ib 'glad of heart'; Budge: net'em) · also the adjective used as a noun, 'the sweet one'
glossary.sḫr: sḫr — to overthrow, fell (causative verb, from ḫr 'fall'); to harm, bring to ruin (?) (sense uncertain) · a second word of the same spelling: plan, counsel, design (noun m.; plural sḫrw; Budge: seχeru)
glossary.nfrw: nfrw — beauty, goodness (noun; abstract plural of nfr "good, beautiful") · a second word of the same spelling, not understood: perhaps a place in the sun's bark (?) (noun; Budge: neferu, with a query)
glossary.ḏḥwty: ḏḥwty — Thoth, the ibis god of writing, reckoning and wisdom, recorder of the judgement of the dead (god's name; Budge: Teḥuti)
glossary.mꜣꜥt: mꜣꜥt — truth, right order (maꜥat) · also Maat, the goddess of truth and right order (god's name; the seated goddess with the feather)
glossary.ꜥ: ꜥ — arm, hand (noun; dual ꜥwy "the two arms") · a second word of the same spelling: state, condition (noun)
glossary.·sn: ·sn — they, them, their (3rd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.iwi: iwi — to come (verb; participle iw "coming, who comes")
glossary.ḥtp: ḥtp — to be content, at peace, to rest (verb); peace; offering (noun; m ḥtp "in peace") · also, of the sun, to set (verb; ḥtp·f 'his setting')
glossary.sꜥnḫ: sꜥnḫ — to make live, keep alive, nourish (verb; causative of ꜥnḫ 'live'; Budge: seānχ)
glossary.ḥtp-nṯr: ḥtp-nṯr — god's offerings, the offerings of a temple (noun)
glossary.wꜣst: wꜣst — Thebes (place name; Waset; Budge: Uast)
